slots_and_copies.name: slot_1
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Read by FUN_08045958(1) (EEPROM blocks 32-63) and validated by FUN_0804599c; replaces slot 0 in live struct if valid and (no valid slot 0 or (ushort)(slot1_first_u16 - slot0_first_u16) < 0x40). All 0xFF (invalid) in sample.

checksums.name: slot_sum16_zero
checksums.formula_detail: In RAM/logical image (each 8-byte .sav block reversed): stored u16LE at logical 254 (0xFE, word 127) == (-(sum of u16LE words 0..126, logical 0x00..0xFB plus magic word 126)) & 0xFFFF; equivalently sum of all 128 u16LE words over logical 0..255 & 0xFFFF == 0. Validator FUN_0804599c gates on word126==constant (0x55A6 observed) then requires (sum & mask)==0 with mask inferred 0x0000FFFF (literal unresolved; sample sum is 0x00420000). Raw-file equivalent: sum of u16BE over file slot bytes & 0xFFFF == 0. Stored file bytes are at slot file offset 248 (DA 6F) due to per-8-byte block reversal; magic file bytes 55 A6 at slot file offset 250.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 driver (src,dst,count): writes DMA3 SAD/DAD/CNT in 0x040000D4 block (register literals unresolved), sets count|0x80000000, polls busy bit 0x8000, suspends/restores DMA3. Used for both EEPROM command write and data read transfers.

EEPROM read of one 8-byte block: sends two leading 1 bits + address bits MSB-first via DMA to 0x0D000000, DMAs back 0x44 halfwords (4 dummy + 64 data bits, 1 bit per halfword), reconstructs 4 u16 MSB-first and stores them descending at dst+6,+4,+2,+0. This is why each 8-byte .sav block is reversed vs RAM. No EEPROM write counterpart exists in the 172 traced functions.

Slot reader: slot param <<5 gives starting EEPROM block (slot0:0, slot1:32); loops 32 blocks x 8B = 256B into staging buffer; brackets with FUN_0800a868/FUN_0800a874 (audio DMA pause/resume via 0x0806a2c0/0x0806a33c). Returns 0 or 0xFFFFFFFF.
Validator: gate word126 at logical 0xFC == constant (0x55A6 observed), then sum of 128 u16 from word126-126 must satisfy (sum & mask)==0, mask inferred 0xFFFF.

Load/select/commit: reads+validates slot0 then slot1, memcpy (FUN_0806b7d8) 0x74 bytes staging->live per selection rule, then FUN_080457a8 apply. Returns 0 if any slot valid else 0xFFFFFFFF. Caller via func_0x08045a58 (missing from callgraph.json FUN-only edges).
memcpy (dst,src,n). In save path copies 0x74-byte payload staging->live. Role label serialize is structural only; it does not write EEPROM.
Apply live struct: calls FUN_0800b9ac which writes 4 u16s from a byte-indexed table. Does not touch EEPROM.
UNRESOLVED external func_0x0804576c, body absent from corpus. Called after FUN_08045820 sets live byte 0x6B=0xFF. Candidate flush/save writer - HYPOTHESIS only, not verified.

open_questions: EEPROM writer absent: no write-opcode function in 172 traced functions. Is unresolved func_0x0804576c (called from FUN_08045820 after setting byte 0x6B=0xFF) the flush/save routine? Its body and all out-of-trace writers are unknown.

Absolute RAM addresses of staging and live buffers are unresolved (_DAT_080xxxxx literal pools not decoded in decompiled.c); all fields are staging/live base + logical offset. Are the FUN_08045a58, FUN_08045820 and FUN_0800db5c buffers the same live struct?

Exact EEPROM address-bit count and device block limit (bytes at *_DAT_0806b334+8 and *_DAT_0806b298+4 in FUN_0806b280) are unresolved constants; 64 blocks x 8B inferred from FUN_08045958 loop and 512B file.
Checksum mask literal uRam080459d4 in FUN_0804599c is unresolved; 0x0000FFFF inferred because sample sum is 0x00420000 (bits 17 and 22 set, so any mask containing them would fail).
Magic constant _DAT_080459b0 is unresolved; 0x55A6 is the observed word 126 value, not a decoded literal.

Semantics of record numeric fields (logical record +0 bytes, +4 u32LE, +14 u16LE) and config tail bytes (0x54..0x73 except flag 0x6B) are unknown; only bytes/ASCII verified. Single sample cannot show variation.
Generation/selection: is first u16 (logical 0x00, value 0 in sample, incremented by FUN_08045820) truly a sequence counter? Only one populated slot exists; slot1 comparison behaviour is static-only.

Record framing (4-byte header + five 16-byte records at logical 0x04) is forced by name spacing but no code in corpus indexes records by stride; per-field readers (display/options code) are outside the traced set.
When is saving triggered in gameplay (option change, ranking entry, game over)? Not exercised by the frame 1106-1157 paired states; writer hunt requires runtime watch on 0x0D000000 writes.
